title: Building an MCP Client — Discovery, Invocation, Session Management

questions.question: How many canonical tools are present after discovering the three fake servers and prefixing collisions?
questions.explanation: The merged registry keeps seven tools: notes search/create, files search/read, and three GitHub tools with colliding search names prefixed.

questions.question: Where does the canonical files/search name route?
options: The notes server's local search function
files/search -> files.search
The GitHub server's list_issues function
No server; it is a display-only alias
questions.explanation: The prefix identifies the files session while preserving its local tool name search for dispatch.

questions.question: What happens to the first unqualified search name under prefix-on-collision?
options: It is deleted because search is ambiguous
It becomes github/search immediately
The first keeps search; later names are prefixed
All three servers are renamed with numeric suffixes
questions.explanation: The merge policy preserves the first registration as search and qualifies subsequent duplicate names such as files/search and github/search.

questions.question: What does a call to notes create report after the notes session is marked dead?
options: A successful note with a new id
A retry against the files server
A JSON-RPC parse error
isError: session dead: notes
questions.explanation: Session.alive is checked before routing, so a dead session returns an explicit session-dead tool error.

questions.question: What does merge(policy=reject) do when a later server exports an existing name?
options: skip the later duplicate
It sends both calls to the later server
It changes every name to a UUID
It raises before retaining any tools
questions.explanation: The reject policy keeps the first canonical registration and omits later tools whose local name collides.

questions.question: What state does initialize_all record for each successful Session?
options: Only the server name; discovery happens on every call
The server capabilities and alive=True
A permanent OAuth token
A single global tool list with no session identity
questions.explanation: Initialization stores each server's advertised capabilities and marks its session alive before discovery and invocation.
